newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sets high fructose corn syrup import duties.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sets high fructose corn syrup import duties.

text.p: Mexico's Trade Ministry on Wednesday set specific tariffs for high fructose corn syrup for U.S. exporters, to take effect beginning on Thursday.
"The present resolution will take effect the day following its publication in the Official Gazette," the ministry wrote in the gazette.
The ministry said it will levy a $63.42 tariff per tonne duty on grade 55 (55 percent fructose) HFCS and a $66.57 per tonne tariff on grade 42 (42 percent fructose) HFCS from Cargill Inc.
For AE Staley Manufacturing Co, the U.S.-based unit of Tate & Lyle, the duty was set at $95.58 per tonne of grade 55 and $125.30 per tonne of grade 42.
Archer Daniels Midland Co (ADM) 's tariffs were $65.12 per tonne for grade 55 and $77.25 per tonne for grade 42 for the sweetener.
All other U.S. exporters of grade 55 HFCS named in the dumping decision, including CPC International, were given a tariff of $175.50 per tonne, the gazette said.
For all other U.S. exporters of grade 42 HFCS, including CPC, the tariff was set at $125.30 per tonne, it said.

"Importers of identical or similar merchandise to high fructose corn syrup are not obligated to pay the tariffs...if they can prove that the country of origin is not the United States," the ministry wrote in the report.
It said in the report that the U.S. HFCS exports have grown to Mexico in recent years, "because of the dynamic performance of the Mexican bottling industry...and Mexico's high soda consumption."

"The ministry concluded that the freely disposable capacity of high fructose corn syrup in the U.S. industry indicates the founded possibility of a substantial increase in exports in conditions of price discrimination in the Mexican market."
The ministry said interested parties had 30 working days from the publication of the tariffs to object to the duties formally with the Mexican government.
